The '''battle systems''' are the core engine for battles in the [[Final Fantasy series|''Final Fantasy'' series]]. The first few games had relatively simple battle systems that were developed and built upon as the series grew, with different elements being added and removed as the series progressed. They generally make up a large part of the game and allow the party to increase their strength, learn new abilities, gain new items and advance in the storyline.

A typical battle screen displays the party and the enemies with a background to show the surrounding area. There is a list of the enemies, a list of [[party]] members, and the basic statistics used in combat for each unit that can encompass [[HP (stat)|HP]], [[MP (stat)|MP]], and various other gauge levels.

The series started with a turn-based battle system, that evolved into the Active Time Battle (ATB). Mainline games from ''[[Final Fantasy IV]]'' to ''[[Final Fantasy IX]]'' used variations of ATB, and every mainline game from ''[[Final Fantasy X]]'' through ''[[Final Fantasy XVI]]'' has used a unique battle system, taking and using elements from different battle systems.
{{See|Battle (term)}}

==Types==
===Traditional turn-based===
[[File:FF1Battle.png|thumb|180px|The first battle system from ''[[Final Fantasy]]''.]]
The original turn-based battle system was designed by [[Hiroyuki Ito]] and [[Akitoshi Kawazu]].<ref name="1up Akitoshi Kawazu">[[#Parish October 15 2012|Parish October 15 2012]]</ref><ref name="1up Ito Science of Battle">[[#Parish October 22 2012|Parish October 22 2012]]</ref> It is used in the first three ''[[Final Fantasy series|Final Fantasy]]'' games and ''[[Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light]]''. When encountering [[Random encounter|random enemies]] or bosses, the field screen fades out into a battle screen. On each turn, party members are chosen to perform an action from their available options (such as [[Attack (command)|Fight]], [[Magic (command)|Magic]], or [[Item]]s).

When all party members have chosen their action, each party member and enemy will perform their respective actions in a particular order influenced by their [[Speed (stat)|Agility]] or [[Speed (stat)|Speed]] statistics. The battle round ends when all combatants have performed their selected actions. Thus, Agility does not determine how often a character can act so much as when during a round their actions will take place. In some games, Agility also influences the number of [[Weapon (equipment)|weapon]] strikes a character can land using a single [[Attack (command)|Attack]] command.

===Active Time Battle===
[[File:FFIV Fight.jpg|thumb|200px|ATB as seen in the GBA version of ''[[Final Fantasy IV]]''.]]
{{main|Active Time Battle}}
The '''Active Time Battle (ATB)''' system was introduced in ''[[Final Fantasy IV]]'' and designed by Hiroyuki Ito.<ref name="pcgamer patented mechanics">[[#Peel 2021|Peel 2021]]</ref><ref name="rock paper shotgun">[[#Morton 2021|Morton 2021]]</ref> It is a pseudo-turn based system that adds the dimension of timing for commands. An ATB gauge tracks when party members are going to act. When the gauge is full, members perform an action. In some games, some actions have an additional wait time, such as casting spells or using special abilities. After the action is executed, the ATB gauge is depleted and must recharge. The rate which the gauge recharges typically correlates to the Speed stat of the character and the [[Battle Speed]], which can be adjusted in the [[config]]. Thus combatants do not always get an equal number of actions.

ATB introduced [[attack formations]], an element on how the battle itself is played out. For example, Preemptive Strike and Back Attack change how the battle begins by giving an initial edge to one side or the other by giving them an extra turn or changing the party order to disadvantage them. Side Attack and Pincer Attack change the entire combat, providing more opportunities for strategy.

There are usually two ATB settings available: Active mode and Wait mode. In Active mode, time will seldom stop flowing in battle, if at all. In Wait mode, time stops more often, such as when the player is navigating [[menu]]s. ''[[Final Fantasy VII]]'' and ''[[World of Final Fantasy]]'' each feature a third, intermediate mode called Recommended in the former game and Semi-Active in the latter. Changing the ATB setting is usually the closest thing to changing the in-game difficulty, as some events can be stalled to an extent in Wait mode. One example is stalling the status ailment [[Doom (status)|Doom]], in which the player can let long actions play out while waiting in a menu to pause the counter, only to quickly input actions and stop in another menu later. This can effectively extend seconds of gameplay duration to minutes.

Active Time Battle is used as the main battle system from ''Final Fantasy IV'' to ''Final Fantasy IX'', as well as in non-mainline games including ''[[Final Fantasy X-2]]'' (which introduces [[Chain (term)|Chaining]] attacks) and ''World of Final Fantasy''. The ATB gauge returns in various other battle systems since that are not entirely Active Time Battle systems.

===Charge Time Battle===
[[File:FFT CTB.png|180px|thumb|The Charge Time Battle system, dictating the order of turns.]]
{{Main|Charge time#Final Fantasy Tactics|t1=CT in Final Fantasy Tactics}}
''[[Final Fantasy Tactics]]'' introduced the '''Charge Time Battle (CTB)''' system, created by [[Hiroyuki Ito]] and [[Yasumi Matsuno]]. In this system, [[charge time]] (CT) meters fill up to 100 to allow each unit to take action. The system has since been used in a modified form in ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics Advance]]'' and ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift]]''.
{{clear}}

===Conditional Turn-Based Battle===
[[File:FFXBattle.jpg|thumb|180px|The CTB from ''Final Fantasy X''. Note the Act List on the right.]]
{{Main|Final Fantasy X battle system}}
The '''Conditional Turn-Based Battle''' system, or the '''Count Time Battle''' system in Japan, designed by [[Toshiro Tsuchida]] is used in ''[[Final Fantasy X]]''. CTB is a turn-based system which does not operate in rounds, instead it uses an Act List that is affected through various means and thus does not guarantee that each participant in a battle will have an equal number of turns. Units with higher speed take more turns than slower ones, making speed more important than in other turn-based battle systems. Players can substitute party members mid-battle adding a new level of strategy.

Spells and abilities (such as [[Haste (Final Fantasy X)|Haste]] or [[Overdrive (Final Fantasy X)|Overdrives]]) modify the Act List, as some abilities require a longer cooldown time. Weaker abilities tend to require less cooldown, thus introducing a trade-off between speed and power. When a character's turn begins, all action stops while the player decides upon an action. This shifts the focus from reflexes and quick decision-making to strategy and careful planning.

The Conditional Turn-Based Battle system is the battle system of ''[[Final Fantasy Dimensions II]]'' and ''[[Dissidia Final Fantasy Opera Omnia]]''.

===Real Time Battle===
[[File:FFXI Battle.jpg|thumb|180px|A Real Time Battle in ''Final Fantasy XI'' between a party of two players and one foe.]]
The '''Real Time Battle (RTB)''' system was introduced in ''[[Final Fantasy XI]]'' and was designed by [[Akihiko Matsui]], who created the battle system for ''Chrono Trigger''. The RTB system replaces the random encounter that featured in past ''Final Fantasy'' games, and instead monsters freely roam areas and are seamlessly engaged.

As the battle takes place without a separate battle screen loading, one is free to move around the landscape during battles, interact with other players, or avoid battles altogether. Monsters may attack players without provocation, retaining a hint of random encounters. Characters start attacking automatically once they are in combat with an enemy, and special commands and magic can be input any time. Many items, spells and abilities used during battle have a casting time or delay to use once activated, similar to Active Time Battles.

An variant form of the RTB system was used in [[Final Fantasy XIV (version 1.0)|the original release of ''Final Fantasy XIV'']].

===Active Dimension Battle===
[[File:Bagoly.jpg|thumb|180px|Active Dimension Battle in ''[[Final Fantasy XII]]''.]]
{{main|Final Fantasy XII battle system}}
The '''Active Dimension Battle (ADB)''' system is meant to be an evolution of the Active Time Battle (ATB) system. The system was designed and directed by [[Hiroyuki Ito]], with the actual programming being done by Takashi Isowaki under [[Takashi Katano]].{{cite|Final Fantasy XII Battle Ultimania|p=207|name=ff12_ultimania}} ADB was only used in ''[[Final Fantasy XII]]''. The ADB system eliminates random battles; the battles take place on the field with no separate battle screen and as such there is no transition between exploration and battle.

The player has the choice of confronting enemies or keeping their distance and exploring the area. Some creatures will not instigate battle with the party unless the party attacks first, and some enemies encountered on the field will be far too powerful when the party first meets them, adding an element of risk to an all-out-attack methodology when first exploring areas. The player has control over a single party member's movement while engaged in battle and the distance between party members and enemies influences battles as various spells and abilities have an [[Area of Effect]] (AoE), meaning party members and enemies need to be within a certain range of each other for the abilities to hit.

Due to the addition of a Turbo mode, which is activated by holding down the {{button|ps|l1}} button, the iteration of ADB used in ''[[Final Fantasy XII#International Zodiac Job System|Final Fantasy XII International Zodiac Job System]]'' and ''The Zodiac Age'' is the fastest battle system in the series.

===Command Synergy Battle===
[[File:FFXIII-gameplay.jpg|thumb|180px|A Command Synergy Battle in ''Final Fantasy XIII''.]]
{{Main|Command Synergy Battle}}
'''Command Synergy Battle (CSB)''' is the battle system in ''[[Final Fantasy XIII]]'' and ''[[Final Fantasy XIII-2]]'' designed by [[Toshiro Tsuchida]], the creator of the Conditional Turn-Based Battle (CTB) system. It derives the flow of time from ATB as each party member has a unique ATB gauge that acts like an action point meter divided up into equal sections (a similar system was used in Enix's game ''[[wikipedia:Robotrek|Robotrek]]''). Each action consumes a portion of the ATB gauge; for example, using [[Commando (Final Fantasy XIII)#Attack|Attack]] consumes one segment, while casting [[Ravager (Final Fantasy XIII)#Firaga|Firaga]] consumes three. Commands can be chained so as long as there are enough ATB segments. When the player decides on what commands to take, they press another button to execute the commands. If the player executes the chained commands without filling all ATB slots, the unused slots will be filled at the start of the next turn.

Unlike regular ATB, the player is only able to control the actions of the party leader. The party begins with two ATB segments, and each gain a segment through story progression at the end of Chapter Two, subduing their respective [[Eidolon (Final Fantasy XIII)|Eidolon]], obtaining the unique ATB crystal on their [[Crystarium system|Crystarium]] tree, and synthesizing a third tier [[Final Fantasy XIII weapons|weapon]], for a maximum of six segments. In ''Final Fantasy XIII-2'', two ATB segments can be gained through completing a Crystarium Level and selecting to gain an extra segment. A final segment can be obtained through [[Ultimate weapon (term)|ultimate weapons]]. In both games, obtaining extra segments means that, although the entire gauge takes longer to recharge, individual segments refill faster. At six ATB segments, each segment recharges almost twice as fast as having two.

At the end of the battle, the player is judged on a rating of zero to five stars in the [[Battle Results#Final Fantasy XIII|Battle Results]] screen. In ''Final Fantasy XIII'', the rating is based on a comparison between the party's power and battle duration, while in ''Final Fantasy XIII-2'', only battle duration is ranked. Battle ranking determines rate and quality of spoils and, in some specific battles, obtaining the highest rank will unlock its trophy.

====Style-Change Active Time Battle====
[[File:LRFFXIII Style-Change.png|thumb|180px|Lightning changing her Schema mid-battle.]]
'''Style-Change Active Time Battle (SATB)''' is the battle system in ''[[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII]]''. It is an evolved version of Command Synergy Battle and was created by [[Yuji Abe]].

The base idea of the battle system was to shuffle through equipment and ability sets on the go, while retaining the action style of Command Synergy Battle. An early glimpse of this battle system is present in the ''[[Lightning's Story: Requiem of the Goddess]]'' DLC scenario for ''Final Fantasy XIII-2''.

As opposed to Command Synergy Battle where a party of maximum three members could participate, the Style-Change Active Time Battle allows for a single character to be present on the battlefield. [[Lightning (Final Fantasy XIII)|Lightning]], the sole playable character of ''Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII'', can shift between three [[schema]]ta to which a player can assign various equipment pieces and [[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII abilities|abilities]]. Each schema has an ATB gauge which fills over time, and the recharge rate is accelerated when the schema is inactive. For each schema, up to four actions are assigned to the four face buttons. Using an individual action costs a portion of the active schema's ATB gauge. Lightning will always begin battle in the schema that the player has set as the default, and her appearance outside of battle is also based on her default schema.

Lightning can freely move around the battlefield at a rate of 1.8 meters per second, or 20 meters when running towards an enemy after executing a physical attack from a distance. Using the [[Fatal Sweep (Lightning Returns)|Fatal Sweep]] and [[Evade (Lightning Returns)|Evade]] abilities allows her to quickly move backwards, or in the direction of the movement stick. She can deal extra damage to enemies by striking from the side or behind. Some enemies have breakable appendages, which increases [[Item drop|drop rates]].

As another new element, Lightning can spend [[Energy Points]] during battle to perform special actions. Such actions include casting [[Curaga (Lightning Returns)|Curaga]] or [[Quake (Lightning Returns)|Quake]], recovering from [[Knocked Out|KO]] with [[Arise (Lightning Returns)|Arise]], using [[Overclock (Lightning Returns)|Overclock]] to slow down time in order to deal heavy damage and more easily stagger enemies, and using her [[Army of One (Lightning Returns)|Army of One]] attack. A portion of the EP gauge is refilled at the end of every battle, with the amount refilled detailed on the battle ranking screen.

===Active X Battle===
The '''Active X Battle (AXB)''' system, pronounced "Active Cross Battle", is the battle system of ''[[Final Fantasy XV]]'' designed by [[Takatsugu Nakazawa]]. Players come into contact with enemies on the field. When an enemy targets the player, an encounter gauge appears on the screen, giving the player chance to flee before it fills and avoid the battle. The player can also initiate battles with the enemies on the field without waiting for them to target them first. There is a chance nearby enemies from the field will join in the battle once one has been initiated.

The player controls one character with the other party members being controlled by the AI. The player's actions are assigned to the controller's face buttons, with one button assigned for special moves, one for attacking, and one for defending and evading. Defending, evading, and using abilities consumes MP. HP and MP slowly recover over time. The player can also perform counterattacks by timing their parries precisely; enemies have a visual cue on when they are going to use an especially strong attack, signaling to either counter or evade.

If the player falls to 0 HP, they enter "[[Final Fantasy XV statuses#Danger|Danger]]" status and have a limited time to heal before they are KO'd. The game is over if the controllable character gets KO'd, but there is still a window for using a revival item. The default player character is [[Noctis (Final Fantasy XV party member)|Noctis]], but the others can be unlocked in the [[Ascension (Final Fantasy XV)|Ascension]] grid, though character-swap is not always available. Every playable character has their own battle style. Noctis's special ability is [[Armiger]], while the others use [[Technique (Final Fantasy XV)|Technique]]s. The player can swap weapons on-the-fly, and Noctis can equip four weapons at once, with the weapon slots also being used for magic.

===Unnamed ''Final Fantasy VII Remake Series'' system===
{{Main|Final Fantasy VII Remake battle system|Final Fantasy VII Rebirth battle system}}
In the ''[[Final Fantasy VII Remake Series]]'', the battle system retains Active Time Battle aspects, although it is action-based to retain strategy elements. The combat is now in real time as long as Tactical Mode is not active. The playable character dodges, blocks and attacks in real time. Normal attacks have two modes, for example, [[Cloud Strife (VII Remake party member)|Cloud]] can switch between the [[Operator Mode (VII Remake)|Operator]] and [[Punisher Mode (VII Remake)|Punisher Mode]]s for light and heavy attacks respectively. Normal attacks do not deal lots of damage, but fill up the two ATB bars faster than they'd fill up over time by themselves. If an ATB segment is full, the player can enter Tactical Mode to slow time to a crawl and choose actions from the Command Menu, such as special abilities, casting spells, and using items. Using an item will use one ATB charge. Commands can also be bound to shortcuts and used quickly without the need for Tactical Mode.

Every enemy has a focus gauge that fills up when they take damage. When full, the enemy will become [[Stagger (VII Remake)|staggered]] and take bonus damage.

Switching between characters in combat only takes one button press, and they will continue to fight on their own when not controlled directly.

===Unnamed ''Final Fantasy XVI'' battle system===
Described by the game's developers as the first "true" action RPG in the series, the battle system in ''[[Final Fantasy XVI]]'' focuses heavily on real-time combat and player control, eschewing command and menu driven combat completely, and was designed by [[Ryota Suzuki]], taking queues and inspirations from his earlier works like ''Devil May Cry'' and ''Dragon's Dogma''.

The player solely controls [[Clive Rosfield]] directly, with different moves being assigned to different face buttons. Clive can be equipped with different [[Eikon]]s, which determine what moves are possible at a time. Up to three different Eikons can be equipped at once, swappable at the press of a button, allowing for different move loadouts that can be chained in sequence. 

Clive can be made to Attack with the left face button and jump with the bottom face button. Each Eikon's base commands are equivalent between them, with an elemental ranged magic set to the the top face button, and a special Eikon ability set to the right face button. The functionality of the attacks and magical attacks can change depending on the sequence of buttons pressed or the player character's condition (airborne, having just avoided an attack, etc.) Additionally, four special abilities can be equipped for each Eikon, accessed by holding the second right trigger button, replacing the functionality of the face buttons with the equipped moves. Clive can be made to dodge enemy attacks by pressing the first right trigger button, and if timed properly can enter a special state that allows different moves properties to change.

The battle system also features usable items, equipped to three slots and seamlessly usable during gameplay by pressing up, right, or down, on the directional pad. Additionally, when accompanied by the wolf companion [[Torgal]], the player will be able to perform 3 orders, requesting an attack, healing or assistance. This is done by pressing  up, right, or down, on the directional pad. Changing between items and Torgal commands is done by pressing left on the directional pad.

The battle system features no [[MP (stat)|MP]], instead limiting the usage of Eikon special abilities by cooldowns, observable in the HUD even when not equipped with the Eikon. The battle system features no player control when it comes to party members, with the player unable to equip or instruct party members to perform actions, besides the aforementioned Torgal. Instead party members are AI controlled and able to perform their own attacks on their own timing, although they will attempt to coordinate their attacks with the player's. Party members have no [[HP (stat)|HP]] and do minimal damage on their own, even on staggered enemies.

Larger enemies in the game feature a [[Will Gauge]] situated below their HP bar, which when depleted, will trigger a [[Stagger]], during which the enemy will be unable to attack and will receive additional damage. Larger enemies can also feature separate hurtboxes for parts of their body (such as paws, tails, or heads) which can be targeted individually by certain abilities or manually by focusing attacks. These parts of the body can have different defense values, allowing the player to hurt enemies more or less depending on the targeted body part.

The battle system features no elemental weakness or strengths, as part of a desire from the developers' to not limit player's choices with regards to Eikon choice.

Occasionally, battles will be faced between full-sized Eikons, leading to the player controlling Clive transformed into [[Ifrit (Final Fantasy XVI)|Ifrit]]. These battles adapt the main combat system to a larger scale, with Ifrit sharing most functionality with Clive, with recovery "items" usable with the directional pad, a melee attack on the left face button, a jump command on the bottom face button, a projectile attack on the top face button, and a special ability on the right face button. Special abilities unique to Ifrit can also be used.
